acts.title: Should secondary schools start the day at ten o’clock?
parts: 1 · the question, and what the essay will do
text: Several countries have now moved the start of the school day from eight to ten o’clock. This essay considers the main advantages and disadvantages of the change.

On the one hand, there are two significant benefits. One major advantage is biological: teenagers genuinely fall asleep later than adults, and the research on this is not seriously disputed. Schools that have made the change report better attendance and fewer late arrivals. A second advantage is that the roads are quieter at ten, which makes the journey both faster and safer.

On the other hand, the drawbacks are practical rather than scientific, which does not make them small. A significant drawback is childcare: most parents start work at eight or nine, so a later start leaves two hours in which younger children in the same family have nowhere to be. There is also the end of the day. If school finishes at five, evening sport, music lessons and part-time jobs all move into the dark, and in a northern winter that is not a minor detail.
It is worth noting that the two sides are not equally easy to fix. The biological argument cannot be changed, whereas the childcare problem can be solved with a supervised room and a small budget.

All things considered, the advantages outweigh the disadvantages, provided that the school is prepared to open its building at eight for the families who need it. Without that, the change simply moves a problem from the students to their parents.

acts.title: Argued out loud, or written down?
text: In a debate you can interrupt, agree partly, and change your mind in front of the other person. Short phrases do most of the work.
An essay has to make both cases fairly before it chooses. It uses written linkers, no contractions, and never addresses the reader directly.

write.q: This is the last piece of writing of the level. Write an advantages-and-disadvantages essay of about 250 words on a question that is actually being argued about where you live. Follow the model: the question and what the essay will do → the advantages with evidence → the disadvantages, taken seriously → weigh the two sides → conclude, with a condition if you need one.
plan: the question + what the essay will do
write.model:
Several employers in the city have now moved to a four-day week on full pay. This essay considers the main advantages and disadvantages of the change.

On the one hand, there are two significant benefits. One major advantage is that the companies which have tried it report almost no fall in output: the work simply expands less. A second advantage is recruitment. In a market where wages are broadly similar, a free Friday is the only offer that costs a company nothing and is understood by everybody.

On the other hand, the drawbacks are real. A significant drawback is that it does not transfer. A shop, a hospital or a bus route cannot close on Friday, so the benefit goes to office workers and to almost nobody else, which widens a gap that is already wide. There is also the question of what happens to the same volume of work in fewer hours: several employees I have spoken to said their four days had become considerably heavier than their five.

It is worth noting that the first drawback is structural, whereas the second is a management problem and can be fixed.

All things considered, I would support the change, provided that companies reduce the volume of work rather than compressing it. Without that condition, a four-day week is simply a five-day week with worse Thursdays.

speak.q: Now the debate, and the last spoken task of the level. Take the side you did NOT argue in your essay, and defend it out loud for about a minute. Use “On the one hand… On the other hand…”, agree partly where the other side is right, and finish with “All things considered…”.
speak.model: Right — I’ll take the other side. On the one hand, I completely accept that output doesn’t fall; the evidence is clear and I’m not going to argue with it. On the other hand, a significant drawback is that this only works for people who sit at desks. A hospital can’t close on Friday. So we would be giving an extra day to the people who already have the most control over their week, and nothing at all to the people who have the least. I agree up to a point that management can fix the workload problem. But it can’t fix that one. All things considered, I’d want it for everybody or for nobody.
